definitions.gloss: not to believe what one hears
definitions.explanation: To be so surprised or shocked by something heard that one wonders whether one heard it right. Said of news, a remark or an announcement.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{知|し}らせ→知らせ：03252_shirase⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{耳|みみ}を{疑|うたが}った。
examples.english: I couldn't believe the news when I heard it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{合格|ごうかく}した→合格する：27949_goukakusuru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{電話|でんわ}→電話：01471_denwa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{聞|き}いた→聞く：00483_kiku⟧とき、⟦{思|おも}わ→思う：00492_omou⟧ず⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{耳|みみ}を{疑|うたが}った。
examples.english: When I heard on the phone that I'd passed, I couldn't believe my ears.

notes:
Nearly always in the past tense, {耳|みみ}を{疑|うたが}った, for a reaction to news already heard. It works for good surprises and bad ones.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{思|おも}わ→思う：00492_omou⟧ず{耳|みみ}を{疑|うたが}う: can hardly believe one's ears
- ⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{耳|みみ}を{疑|うたが}う: to doubt one's own ears
- X⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{耳|みみ}を{疑|うたが}う: to be stunned by X (heard)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{目|め}を{疑|うたが}う→目を疑う：31587_mewoutagau⟧: to doubt one's eyes — the same reaction to something seen
